keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, confidence 2: Cliopatria has no 1863 shape, but the Second Mexican Empire page dates the Regency of the Empire to 11 July 1863, and the French intervention page has the French in Mexico City (10 June 1863) and Puebla (17 May 1863). Radii around the two cities stand for the land held at the start; the towns taken in November and December 1863 are ledger events.

232,312 km2; neither page gives an area (the Second Mexican Empire page has a map of 'territory administered' and 'territory claimed' in April 1864, not readable here). The outline is a patchwork of 777 cells: all of the Federal District, most of Veracruz (64 percent), Puebla (59), Guanajuato (62), Aguascalientes (68), Jalisco (45), México (48), Querétaro (38), Zacatecas (36), Tabasco (36), Campeche (22), Durango (14), and little of Michoacán (12), San Luis Potosí (0) or Oaxaca (1). The page says French and imperial forces controlled 'the center of the country, the port of Veracruz, the capital Mexico City, and other major cities as north as Monterrey and as south as Oaxaca', and the French intervention page dates Querétaro, Morelia, Guanajuato, San Luis Potosí and Guadalajara; so the shape matches the page for Veracruz, the centre and Guadalajara and omits San Luis Potosí, Morelia, Oaxaca and Monterrey, while Campeche, Tabasco, Zacatecas and Durango are on no page. Unverified beyond that: page budget. Kept as drawn; the named towns are in the ledger.

ledger.note: 11 July 1863: the Regency of the Mexican Empire is set up in French-held Mexico City. The Second Mexican Empire page's infobox gives 'Establishment of the Regency of the Empire: 11 July 1863' and says 'The Assembly met in July 1863 and resolved to invite Archduke Maximilian to be Emperor of Mexico'; the French intervention page: the French occupied Mexico City on 10 June 1863, named 35 notables on 16 June, and 'On 11 July, the Assembly resolved that Mexico was to be a constitutional monarchy... The executive was then officially changed to the Regency of the Mexican Empire.' The land is the cities' surroundings, a reading.

wars.outcome: The French take Puebla (17 May 1863) and Mexico City (10 June 1863); the Regency of the Empire is set up (11 July 1863); Imperialist forces take Querétaro, Morelia, Guanajuato and San Luis Potosí (November-December 1863) and Guadalajara (5 January 1864); Maximilian accepts the crown on 10 April 1864. The intervention ends in 1867 (infobox 8 December 1861 – 21 June 1867; French withdrawal announced 19 December 1866, Bazaine leaves Mexico City 5 February 1867, the Empire ends 19 June 1867), after this dossier's life.
wars.note: The Tampico entry ('captured by the French Navy on 11 August') has no year on the page and is not used; Monterrey (15 August 1864, Vidaurri's forces) and Oaxaca (end of 1864) fall after this dossier's end and belong to the Second Mexican Empire.

certainty.note: The pages name towns, not frontiers; the front moved with the French columns and the countryside was held by republican guerrillas.

notes: The Cliopatria row 'Mexican Monarchists' (Wikipedia title Conservative Party (Mexico), one shape, 1864) is the territory of the Regency of the Mexican Empire and then Maximilian's Empire in 1864: the Second Mexican Empire page puts the Regency at 11 July 1863 and the acceptance at 10 April 1864, and Cliopatria's 'Second Mexican Empire' row (the whole country, 1865-1867) is the same regime's claim. This dossier is the 1863 – April 1864 stage as its own type-rebel entry (land of the Republic administered under French occupation, hatched); the second-mexican-empire dossier (another part) should list 'Mexican Monarchists' in its cliopatria_names or start in 1864; the Mexico dossier already hands its 1864 shape to second-mexican-empire from April 1864. The year step cannot split 1864: both dossiers draw it. Not settled: the shape's composition (Campeche, Tabasco, Zacatecas, Durango are in it on no page; San Luis Potosí, Morelia and Oaxaca are on the page but outside it); the date of Tampico's capture (page gives '11 August' without year); the Reform War (1857-1860) in which the Conservatives held Mexico City: the Conservative Party page gives only 'lose the war in 1860', no territory, and is not researched here. Page budget: 2 pages allowed, 4 opened (one a disambiguation page opened by mistake) because the Conservative Party page carries no territory. Counterpart second-french-empire (the occupying power) is written by eu-20.
